title: How the macOS accessibility tree works
head: Your apps have a second interface.
dek: AX is what an app tells tools about its buttons and windows.

beats.text: You see a window and an Export button. Accessibility, often shortened to AX, describes those controls to other tools.
That description is a tree. An app contains a window. The window contains controls, such as buttons.
An element can expose its role: Button; its title: Export; and a supported action: Press. A tool can ask the app to press it.
The app decides what it exposes. Some controls may be missing or incomplete. Tools need Accessibility permission to access and control other apps.

title: AX vs screenshots: what UI automation can see
head: Two ways to understand a screen.
dek: A screenshot shows appearance. AX describes exposed controls.

beats.text: A screenshot is an image: shapes, colors, and visible text. A tool must interpret the pixels to locate a button.
AX is structured information supplied by the app. A button may identify its role, title, and supported Press action.
Each view has limits. Pixels do not directly encode a button action. AX can omit a custom control or provide incomplete information.
Use the evidence the app provides, then verify what changed. Accessibility access and Screen Recording are separate macOS permissions.
